finding.evidence: Proof 3.1 says “for s\ge0, w_k^{2s}\ge1, hence the coefficient sequence is in \ell^2 and [F4] gives its unique L^2 representative.” The cited Fourier-basis result [F4] gives a representative in complex L^2. The defined completion is over real trigonometric polynomials with conjugate-symmetric coefficients; the proof does not show that the resulting complex representative is real-valued. Comparing it with its conjugate using Fourier uniqueness would close this small gap.
